result.summary: This is a typical residential street with row houses and sidewalks on both sides. While the environment is low-speed in character, it lacks proactive pedestrian safety features such as marked crossings, traffic calming, or buffers between the walkway and moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates significant sightline obstructions for pedestrians, especially children, attempting to cross the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffers
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalks are immediately adjacent to the travel and parking lanes with no physical buffer or planting strip.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the nearest intersections to improve pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low on this residential stretch.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the street while improving the pedestrian environment.

result.summary: The environment is a narrow residential street that lacks any dedicated pedestrian infrastructure, such as sidewalks or marked crossings. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicles, and sightlines are significantly limited by parked cars and the close proximity of buildings to the street edge.

hazards.name: Lack of dedicated pedestrian space
hazards.description: Pedestrians must walk in the same space as moving vehicles due to the absence of sidewalks.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right side block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven concrete slabs create potential trip hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface in the foreground and midground

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Provide a dedicated, raised walkway for pedestrians to separate them from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain very low in this shared environment.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale lighting to improve visibility and safety during night hours.

result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks on both sides but lacks any formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure or traffic calming measures. The wide, unmarked roadway and presence of large parked vehicles create significant visibility hazards and may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, including a white van and a black pickup truck, block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections or mid-block to reduce crossing distance and bring pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to physically reduce vehicle speeds to levels appropriate for a residential neighborhood.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossing points with high-visibility continental or ladder-style paint to alert drivers to pedestrian activity.

result.summary: This residential mid-block environment features row houses with narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to on-street parking. The pedestrian walkway lacks a buffer from the roadway and is partially obstructed by household items and building steps.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Van
hazards.description: A large white van parked at the curb obscures sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, parked along the curb

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans and building steps encroach on the narrow sidewalk, reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk in front of the row houses

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and parked cars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during evening and night hours.
